messages:
kyle: Heads-up — saw a nasty perf regression on canary when we enabled torch.compile + CUDA graph capture for the long-tail seq lengths. baseline (no compile, no cudagraph): p50=45ms, p95=120ms. compile+cudagraph: p50=38ms but p95 jumped to 340ms. anyone seen this pattern?

jess: @kyle yea saw something similar in nightly. looks like kernel selection during the graph capture path picked different fused kernels that blow up when we hit dynamic seqs. rough logs attached:
```
# capture logs
kernel_pick: aten::matmul -> fused_gemm_sm80 (seq=64)
kernel_pick: aten::matmul -> fused_gemm_sm80 (seq=128)
# later at runtime (replay)
replay_path: seq=256 -> falling back to generic_gemm (slow)
```

lina: fwiw torch.compile's graph capture does shape-specialized lowering. if capture happens on shorter sequences the captured CUDA graph might not include kernels optimized for longer sequences. cudagraph capture also pins kernel choices at capture time.

kyle: so capture time shape distribution matters — we need either: (1) multi-shape warmup/capture, (2) disable cudagraph for dynamic batches, or (3) make kernel selection more conservative during capture. thoughts on cost vs complexity?

jess: we tried multi-shape warmup before. pros: capture paths for all seq buckets. cons: long startup and memory pressure because we cache multiple graphs/kernels. example warmup script we used:
```
for seq in [32,64,128,256]:
    input = rand(batch, seq)
    model(input)  # trigger compile + capture
```
That reduced p95 but increased memory by ~12%.

lina: another angle: change autotuner to be architecture-aware + seq-aware. during capture, tag the graph with a "seq_bucket" and prefer kernels optimized for the bucket family. then on replay, if input falls outside bucket, either trigger quick fallback to interpreter or trigger background re-capture. low-latency fallback keeps tail bounded.

kyle: interesting. we could also make the kernel picker consult runtime histograms: if we've historically seen >10% of requests in a different bucket, expand capture. requires state though.

perf-bot: [perf-alert] 2025-03-22T10:12:45Z — p95 latency spike on canary: +183% after enable-compile flag. Link: https://perf.internal/redwood/canary/1749

jess: profiling traces show heavy time spent in generic_gemm kernel at p95. NVTX shows kernel launch divergence during replay for seq>128. patch suggestion: add an assert in capture code to log if capture_seq != replay_seq (freq) so we can quantify mismatch rate.

lina: code sketch for a conservative capture policy:
```
# pseudo
if dynamic_shapes_detected:
    disable_cudagraph_capture()
else:
    enable_cudagraph_capture()
```
But we prefer auto policy: enable capture only if 95th-percentile of warmup shapes within +-20% of median.

kyle: action items: 1) jess add capture mismatch logging + push to canary (low overhead) 2) lina prototype sequence-bucket metadata and fallback policy 3) run multi-shape warmup experiment on a few model configs (gpt-2 small, llama-ish 7b)

jess: will open PR for logging + a small perf test. I'll include NVTX and a tiny repro that toggles cudagraph.

lina: I'll mock an autotune loop: sample recent seq histogram from router and decide whether to capture multi-shape or fallback. will push a draft by EOD.

kyle: thanks. also let's add a dashboard panel showing "capture_seq vs replay_seq" distribution so SRE can watch. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: branch=canary/compile-capture-logs sha=abc123 -> canary cluster at 2025-03-22T11:00:00Z

jess: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789 — adds capture mismatch logging and tiny repro. note: disabled by default behind feature flag.

kyle: perfect. if we can't get a robust autotune soon, prefer disabling cudagraph for models with >20% seq variance to avoid p95 regressions. :thumbsup:

lina: agree. will include that threshold in my draft.

kyle: thanks all — let's reconvene after canary run (check perf dashboard in ~24h). :rocket:
